results.update: The award was fully executed on September 18 after the carrier's appraiser revised his estimate per our request (supervision hours and downspouts); the file is closed and paid.

timeline.event: File received from the contractor to begin the appraisal process.
Demand for appraisal sent to the carrier.
Carrier acknowledged the demand and said it would follow up.
Carrier said the claim needed to be reopened and asked whether a release had been signed.
Carrier issued a below-deductible letter closing the original claim with no payment, and the file moved to a new claim number.
Appraisal Demand Letter sent to the homeowner to sign under the new claim number.
Homeowner signed the appraisal demand.
Demand for appraisal sent to the carrier under the new claim number.
Contractor's estimate, photos, and demand letter sent to the carrier with the updated claim number.
Carrier confirmed receipt and said to allow 3-4 days for review.
Carrier named its appraiser (Diamond Ross) and requested our office's umpire list and inspection availability.
Carrier's appraiser sent a list of proposed umpire candidates.
Carrier's appraiser provided availability for the inspection on August 14.
Carrier's appraiser agreed to an umpire from the proposed list.
Carrier's appraiser sent appraisal paperwork for signature and confirmed the inspection for August 14 at 9:30 AM.
Homeowner confirmed the schedule for August 14 at 9:30 AM with interior access.
Solo inspection held with the carrier's appraiser, including interior access.
Sent the completed estimate to the carrier's appraiser.
Carrier's appraiser said the position would be ready in a few days and asked for the measurement file.
Followed up with the carrier's appraiser to see if he had reviewed the position sent on August 18.
Carrier's appraiser sent a position estimate and noted it did not include interior scope, since the homeowner reported no interior damage.
Requested additional revisions to the carrier's position (supervision hours and downspouts).
Carrier's appraiser sent a revised estimate and the appraisal award for signature.
Sent the appraisal invoice to the contractor for payment.
Sent the signed appraisal award to the carrier's appraiser.
Carrier's appraiser returned the fully executed appraisal award.

results.update: The signed award was returned to the carrier's appraiser on September 24, following resolution of prior estimate revisions; the appraisal invoice has been paid and the file is closing out.

timeline.event: Carrier's settlement letter arrived paying for only half of the roof replacement, prompting the appraisal.
Contractor asked us to send the homeowner an appraisal demand letter, citing damage to the fence, gutters, outdoor cover, and roof.
Appraisal Demand Letter sent to the contractor for review.
Homeowner approved the demand letter; demand for appraisal sent to the carrier.
Homeowner reported the promised settlement check never arrived.
Contractor confirmed the carrier still had not acknowledged the appraisal; demand for appraisal resent to the carrier.
Homeowner forwarded the original settlement letter again, confirming no check had ever been received.
Asked the carrier to name its appraiser and resent the Appraisal Demand Letter.
Carrier named its appraiser (Kevin Palermo, Compass Adjusting Services).
Requested the carrier's appraiser's availability for a solo inspection.
Selected Shane Sosa as umpire; solo inspection scheduled for September 2, and the homeowner confirmed the appointment.
Signed agreement (Appraiser Declaration) circulated for signatures.
Solo inspection held; sent our position, the estimate, measurement file, and photo report, to the carrier's appraiser.
Requested revisions to the carrier's position; carrier's appraiser agreed to most items but declined supervision hours.
Accepted the carrier's revised position.
Carrier's appraiser sent the award letter for signature.
Appraisal invoice sent to the contractor.
Carrier's appraiser followed up asking whether the award had been signed.
Contractor confirmed the invoice was paid.
Signed award sent back to the carrier's appraiser.

results.update: Joseph served as the umpire on this file. The award was finalized and signed by both party appraisers on September 12; the only outstanding item is Joseph's own signature on the DOA/agreement, which the insured's appraiser flagged on September 14.

timeline.event: Panel reached an impasse; carrier's appraiser sent his position and the signed agreement for the umpire's signature, proposing a panel inspection for July 14.
Insured's appraiser confirmed the July 14 inspection time and sent his supporting position documents.
Insured's appraiser requested the umpire's invoice and W-9.
Umpire accepted the assignment, confirmed no conflicts, and requested each side's full position and supporting documentation.
Umpire's invoice was submitted to the carrier for payment.
Proposed inspecting the property the next day.
Solo inspection scheduled for July 21 at 4:00 PM after a joint inspection date could not be arranged.
Payment for the umpire's inspection was received from the insured.
Followed up requesting the carrier's estimate referencing brick and window damage.
Carrier's appraiser sent the carrier's estimate.
Both party appraisers asked for a timeline to close the appraisal.
Sent our position to the panel; carrier's appraiser flagged missing items (packout/pushback, O&P, chimney, project conditions) and sent his own position.
Insured's appraiser said he had no contest with the umpire's position.
Sent a comparison of both positions, asking the carrier's appraiser for reasoning on the disputed items.
Carrier's appraiser sent his own comparison report justifying the disputed items.
Insured's appraiser asked for a timeline on the final decision.
Sent final rulings on each disputed item and the signed award; both party appraisers returned their signed copies of the award the same day.
Insured's appraiser noted the umpire's own DOA/agreement still needs Joseph's signature.

results.update: Joseph served as the umpire on this file. The appraisal award was finalized and signed by all parties on September 13, closing out a dispute over mitigation costs, cabinet grade, and storage-related contents; the file is complete.

timeline.event: Carrier's appraiser sent his position and notes to the insured's appraiser.
Panel reached an impasse and named Joseph as umpire; Joseph accepted, confirmed no conflicts, and requested invoices be sent.
Insured's appraiser sent his estimate, invoices, and measurement file for review.
Carrier's appraiser sent his estimate, measurement file, notes, and photo report.
Umpire's invoice and W-9 sent; invoice submitted to the carrier for payment.
Proposed a joint inspection given the complexity of the loss; both parties agreed to a solo inspection if needed.
A scheduled solo inspection date fell through; rescheduled toward July 17.
Insured's appraiser sent an updated estimate while working to obtain photos of the stored contents.
Followed up on confirming payment of the umpire invoice.
Began drafting the umpire position, expecting to have it ready within about a week.
Sent our umpire position to the panel; insured's appraiser flagged the kitchen cabinets and tile flooring, and asked that storage-related personal property be handled separately.
Carrier's appraiser raised concerns on cabinet grade, supply lines, and the built-in microwave.
Sent revisions addressing the carrier's appraiser's concerns; insured's appraiser reviewed the estimate and agreed to sign.
Carrier's appraiser raised a discrepancy in the mitigation invoice amount and asked for more documentation.
Carrier's appraiser confirmed with the mitigation contractor that the lower invoice amount was correct and undisputed.
Sent the finalized award for signature; insured's appraiser signed and returned it the same day.
Carrier's appraiser flagged an overhead-and-profit discrepancy on the mitigation line item; discussed reasoning with him.
Sent the signed award letter to all parties, bringing the file to an amicable conclusion.
